## Pre-launch design and preparations

- u4b tracker
  - [u4b_008](/_sources/u4b/u4b_008.qmd)
- Balloon: single [CyMylar 60](/_sources/balloons/cymylar60.qmd) — first flight on this balloon type, chosen over 32in latex for the much higher predicted float
- 97% helium fill; see the fill plan in the u4b_008 notes below
- HF antenna — 20m band
- GPS antenna
- WSPR channel 122 (2-minute transmit slot)

## Launch checklist

### Pre-launch

- [x] weigh payload
- [x] confirm balloon fill plan
- [x] ground test tracker (decoded cleanly on the main receiver once sun was strong; see Ground test log in the u4b_008 notes below)

### At launch site

- [x] wait for a calm lull — wind was higher than preferred for most of the day
- [x] verify WSPR transmissions on ground with SDR Rx
- [x] launch

## Outcome

Both u4b_007 and u4b_008 worked and decoded cleanly on the ground right up to launch (an early ground test attempt failed to decode, but that was attributed to low sun rather than a tracker problem — see the Ground test log below). No telemetry was received from u4b_008 after launch. The leading theory is antenna damage during the launch release — wind conditions were higher than ideal, which may have caused the HF antenna wire to snag or break as the balloon went up.
